Palmer was a controversial omission from England's World Cup squad in the summer, with an injury-hit season impacting his form. After a summer off, it appeared Palmer was returning to a high level in the early weeks of this campaign, with six goal involvements in seven games for Chelsea. That output earned him a recall to the England group for the Nations League matches with Spain, Czech Republic and Croatia - but Palmer withdrew from the squad due to injury. messages.text: Hain leads Warwickshire's bid for title-clinching win over Leicestershire

metadata.summary: Sam Hain struck a superb 142 to nudge Warwickshire closer to the Rothesay County Championship title as they lead Leicestershire by 192 runs at Edgbaston at the end of day two.
metadata.content: County Championship: Sam Hain leads Warwickshire's bid for title-clinching win over Leicestershire at Edgbaston | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Sam Hain leads Warwickshire's bid for title-clinching win over Leicestershire at Edgbaston Friday's County Championship sees Warwickshire move ever closer to title after moving into lead of 192 runs against relegation-threatened Leicestershire at Edgbaston at the end of day two; Warwickshire win would guarantee a first title since the Covid-shortened 2021 campaign Friday 25 September 2026 20:22, UK Image: Sam Hain produced 142 with the bat to push Warwickshire ever closer to the County Championship title Sam Hain struck a superb 142 to nudge Warwickshire closer to the Rothesay County Championship title as they lead Leicestershire by 192 runs at Edgbaston at the end of day two. Warwickshire needed at least 14 points from their final match of the season and have already taken six bonus points after skittling Leicestershire for 125 on day one before Hain led the home side to 372 all out in reply. Leicestershire, who slipped to 55-3 in their second innings at close, are all but relegated, subject to their appeal against a 27-point deduction for a substandard pitch at Grace Road last month. Second-placed Somerset's title hopes appear over - they began their last fixture 11 points behind Warwickshire - even if they beat Surrey at Taunton. messages.text: Talk Of New York shines in Joel Stakes

metadata.summary: Talk Of New York was the chatter of Newmarket as he stared alongside Rebel’s Romance’s brother Fortitudine in a big-race double for Charlie Appleby on the Rowley Mile.
metadata.content: Talk Of New York and Fortitudine star at Newmarket on another good afternoon for Charlie Appleby | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Talk Of New York and Fortitudine star at Newmarket on another good afternoon for Charlie Appleby Godolphin enjoyed a successful day on the Rowley Mile on Friday with Talk Of New York returning to winning ways in the Joel Stakes and Fortitudine making it three from three in the Godolphin Stakes Friday 25 September 2026 17:17, UK Image: A general view of Talk Of New York ridden by William Buick (right) on their way to winning the Betway Joel Stakes Talk Of New York was the chatter of Newmarket as he stared alongside Rebel’s Romance’s brother Fortitudine in a big-race double for Charlie Appleby on the Rowley Mile. Always held in high regard and third in the St James's Palace Stakes behind Bow Echo and Gstaad, the son of Wootton Bassett was the 4-9 favourite for the Betway Joel Stakes, despite blotting his copybook at Goodwood last time out. Always prominent in the group racing on the stands side, he moved powerfully to the lead under William Buick inside the final furlong, galloping out to a commanding four-and-three-quarter-length success. Appleby, who is continuing in red-hot form, said: "On what he achieved in the St James's Palace you had to come here with confidence and you had to put a line through Goodwood, it was just one of those days and we've been there before. messages.text: 'They changed the plan' - Hamilton left frustrated by Ferrari tactics

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton expressed frustration with Ferrari's approach to Q3 after qualifying sixth for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, saying "they changed the plan".
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says 'they changed the plan' in Azerbaijan GP Qualifying after tow-less Q3 leaves him sixth | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says 'they changed the plan' in Azerbaijan GP Qualifying after tow-less Q3 leaves him sixth Ferrari completing only one multi-lap run in Q3 questioned by Lewis Hamilton after he was left without a tow; But Charles Leclerc on front row in hope for Scuderia; watch the Azerbaijan GP on Saturday at 12pm with build-up from 10.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Friday 25 September 2026 19:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was left frustrated after he could only qualify sixth for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. Lewis Hamilton expressed frustration with Ferrari's approach to Q3 after qualifying sixth for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, saying "they changed the plan". Hamilton questioned why the team completed only one run of multiple laps at the end of the final knockout stage rather than go out earlier for initial laps, as Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull with Max Verstappen had done. The seven-time world champion said his final laps were compromised by having no 'tow' from a car in front to aid straight-line speed down Baku's long main straight. Team-mate Charles Leclerc did have a tow, from Hamilton, by dint of the fact it was the Monegasque's turn to go out second in final qualifying. Azerbaijan GP schedule: Why is the race on Saturday? The Old Firm sides have also challenged the £100,000 sum they were ordered to pay the opposition club for that match. The punishment ruled a second match would be behind closed doors if there is any trouble at a Scottish Cup fixture until the end of next season. metadata.content: Open de France: England's Matt Fitzpatrick grabs halfway lead over Jeff Winther on DP World Tour at Le Golf National | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Open de France: England's Matt Fitzpatrick grabs halfway lead over Jeff Winther on DP World Tour at Le Golf National Matt Fitzpatrick holds a one-shot lead over Jeff Winther, with defending champion Michael Kim two back; Victor Perez fired a hole-in-one during his second round at Le Golf National; watch live on Saturday from midday on Sky Sports Golf Friday 25 September 2026 19:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the second round of the FedEx Open de France, where Matt Fitzpatrick edged ahead England's Matt Fitzpatrick continued his bogey-free start at the FedEx Open de France to charge into the halfway lead at Le Golf National. Fitzpatrick followed Thursday's blemish-free 65 by carding an eagle and five birdies in a seven-under 64 on Friday afternoon, lifting him to 13 under and one ahead of Jeff Winther. Both Fitzpatrick and Winther equalled the lowest round of the day to ensure they would be part of the final group on Saturday, while overnight leader Michael Kim - the defending champion - is two behind after a three-under 68. messages.text: Blow for Littler as new TV major announced and France lands 2027 ranking event

metadata.summary: The introduction of the European Open and a first-ever PDC European Tour event in France will headline a packed 2027 PDC calendar – but the changes could make Luke Littler’s bid to complete darts even harder.
metadata.content: Darts set for major 2027 shake-up with new TV major and France hosting ranking event – but what does it mean for Luke Littler? | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Darts set for major 2027 shake-up with new TV major and France hosting ranking event – but what does it mean for Luke Littler? The PDC European Tour will visit France for the first time next year in Lievin, just a few kilometres from Lens in northern France, as well as the introduction of the European Open; you can watch World Grand Prix Darts live on Sky Sports from September 28 - October 4 Friday 25 September 2026 16:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love the Darts, Michael Bridge, Polly James and Paul Nicholson discuss the whistling aimed at Luke Littler at the World Series of Darts Finals The introduction of the European Open and a first-ever PDC European Tour event in France will headline a packed 2027 PDC calendar – but the changes could make Luke Littler’s bid to complete darts even harder. A significant addition to the 2027 PDC calendar will see the inaugural European Open take place in Salzburg from June 18-20. The new three-day event will follow the World Cup of Darts, which returns to Frankfurt from June 10-13, before the sport heads to Blackpool for the World Matchplay from July 17-25.
